messages.content: Predict a person's time-allocation choice in a decision exercise. Each active group has four members, called union members in the exercise. Each member allocates a total of 40 hours between two activities each round. There are 12 paid rounds, preceded by three unpaid practice rounds. Decisions are made privately and participants must not communicate. The two allocations must sum to 40. The private business activity earns 20 pesos per hour when its return is retained, and zero for the entire private allocation when the adverse draw occurs. The cooperative activity earns every active group member 10 pesos for each hour that any of the four members contributes, including that member's own contribution. Thus each receives 10 times the group's total cooperative hours; there is no additional fixed round payment. This is presented as a lottery over the private return: a losing draw makes it zero and a winning draw retains 20 pesos per private hour. The group total of cooperative hours is announced after choices, while individual choices remain private. Predict the hours allocated to cooperation. The chance of a zero private-business return is announced to the participant before choosing, using a bag of five chips, and is one of 20%, 40%, 60%, or 80%. The random outcome is drawn after the choice. Predict a coarse four-hour range containing the chosen target allocation. Return only one JSON array: [0,4], [4,8], [8,12], [12,16], [16,20], [20,24], [24,28], [28,32], [32,36], or [36,40]. Each returned range includes both endpoints; adjacent ranges may share an endpoint. The original allocation still ranges from 0 to 40 hours. Do not add an explanation.

You are predicting one active member's allocation in this exercise. The supplied information identifies the current zero-return probability as 60% or 80%. The exact current probability, round number, and earlier choice/feedback records are not supplied. The participant was told the actual bag before deciding; missing records do not imply the participant lacked that information. No current choices of other members or outcomes of the forthcoming draw are supplied. Forecast the four-hour range of cooperative hours.

Predict a person's time-allocation choice in a decision exercise. Each active group has four members, called union members in the exercise. Each member allocates a total of 40 hours between two activities each round. There are 12 paid rounds, preceded by three unpaid practice rounds. Decisions are made privately and participants must not communicate. The two allocations must sum to 40. The original allocation still ranges from 0 to 40 hours. Do not add an explanation.

Predict a person's time-allocation choice in a decision exercise. Each active group has four members, called union members in the exercise. Each member allocates a total of 40 hours between two activities each round. There are 12 paid rounds, preceded by three unpaid practice rounds. Decisions are made privately and participants must not communicate. The two allocations must sum to 40. Both activities are private businesses. Activity 1 earns 20 pesos per hour unless an inspection confiscates all its earnings; activity 2 always earns 10 pesos per hour. You also receive a fixed 500 pesos this round, unaffected by anyone's allocation. Your earnings do not depend on the other three active members' choices. Two non-union participants perform a separate task; each hour any active member assigns to activity 1 reduces each of those two people's earnings by 10 pesos. They receive no return from your activity 2 and their choices do not affect your income. A regulation requires all 40 hours in activity 2, but you can choose any allocation. Inspection happens after choices; activity-2 earnings and the fixed amount are retained. Predict the hours allocated to activity 2. The chance of a zero private-business return is announced to the participant before choosing, using a bag of five chips, and is one of 20%, 40%, 60%, or 80%. The random outcome is drawn after the choice. Predict a coarse four-hour range containing the chosen target allocation. Return only one JSON array: [0,4], [4,8], [8,12], [12,16], [16,20], [20,24], [24,28], [28,32], [32,36], or [36,40]. Each returned range includes both endpoints; adjacent ranges may share an endpoint. The original allocation still ranges from 0 to 40 hours. Do not add an explanation.
